text.p: ** BIRTHDAYS **
British novelist ANTHONY TROLLOPE was born in 1815.
Writer MARCUS CLARK, who wrote the Australia epic, "For the term of his natural Life" was born in London in 1846.

French Marshal and politician PHILIPPE PETAIN was born in 1856. After gaining fame in World War One as a masterful general, PETAIN signed the Armistice with the Germans in World War Two. He then became leader of Vichy France, which collaborated with the Nazis. He was imprisoned for life after the war.
WILLIAM JOYCE, the American born British traitor who broadcast propaganda for the Germans in World War Two, was born 1906. The British public derisively called him "Lord Haw-Haw."
Actress SHIRLEY MACLAINE was born in 1934.
BARBRA STREISAND was born in 1942. She won an oscar for the film "Funny Girl".
UK bass player with Jethro Tull, GLEN CORNICK, was born in 1947.
** EVENTS **
1558 : MARY Queen of Scots, aged 16, married the Dauphin
of France, the future FRANCIS II.
1704 : The Boston News-Letter, one of the earliest
newspapers in the American colonies, was first published.
1731 : British journalist and author DANIEL DEFOE, who
wrote "Robinson Crusoe" and "Moll Flanders", died.
1858 : The biggest bell in the world was unveiled in
London. It was hung in the clock tower of Westminister Palace, and within a few years had become known as "Big Ben".
1866 : The Ku Klux Klan was formed in America's south by
angry ex-Confederate officers opposed to black rights.
1916 : The Easter Rising in Dublin, an insurrection aimed
at setting up an Irish Republic, began.
1939 : ROBERT MENZIES became Australian Prime Minister
for the first time.
1945 : U.S. forces liberated Dachau concentration camp.
1950 : The state of Jordan was formed by the union of
Jordanian-occupied Palestine and the Kingdom of Transjordan.
1955 : The Bandung Conference, organised by five Asian
states, ended. It condemned colonialism by both the West and the USSR.
1965 : The government of Indonesia formally took control
of all foreign companies in the country. 1967 : A Russian Soyuz spacecraft crashed killing
astronaut VLADIMIR KOMAROV.
1980 : An attempt by US Special Forces to free 53

Americans held hostage in Iran failed. The mission was abandoned after three of the eight helicopters being used were forced down because of sand storms and mechanical failure. As the Americans prepared to leave one of the remaining helicopters collided with a transport plane killing eight American Servicemen. The debacle virtually destroyed JIMMY CARTER's Presidency. 1986 : WALLIS, Duchess of Windsor, died.
1989 : University researchers in Townsville claimed that
crocodiles were shy and suffered from stress.
1990 : East and West Germany agreed on July 2 as the date
for economic union, a prelude to full political unification.
1993 : A huge IRA bomb exploded in Bishopgate, in the
heart of London's financial district, killing one person. 1996 : The Palestinian parliament-in-exile voted to amend
clauses in the PLO charter which call for Israel's destruction.
